--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.subgraph_isomorphisms()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: List the occurrences of a pattern graph inside this graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.subgraph_isomorphisms()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: List the occurrences of a pattern graph inside this graph. title: >- [Graph.subgraph_isomorphisms()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: List the occurrences of a pattern graph inside this graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} List the occurrences of a pattern graph inside this graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22029-L22209){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.subgraph_isomorphisms( pattern, induced=True, node_attr=None, edge_attr=None, limit=None, symmetry=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Subgraph isomorphisms](../assets/graphs/subgraph-isomorphisms.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: pattern p, a feed-forward loop where A points to B and C and B points to C, beside graph g, a four-node directed network with edges x→y, y→z, x→z, z→w, and y→w. Right: two miniature copies of g, each highlighting one occurrence of the pattern in the accent color, listed beside it: A→x B→y C→z, and A→y B→z C→w." width="100%"} Each occurrence is a mapping from the pattern's nodes to distinct nodes of this graph such that every pattern edge corresponds to an edge here (see `is_subgraph_isomorphic()` for the meaning of `induced=`). Symmetric patterns occur several times on the same nodes: a triangle, for example, is found 6 times on each triangle of the graph, once per way of matching its three corners. Use the mappings to locate motifs, count pattern occurrences, or extract the matched nodes for further analysis. Passing a pattern with the same number of nodes and edges as this graph lists every isomorphism between the two (with `induced=True`), and passing this graph itself lists its automorphisms (symmetries). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `Graph` to search for. It is not modified. [induced]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), require induced occurrences; if `False`, allow extra edges. [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node attribute name, or list of names, whose values must be equal for matched nodes. [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional edge attribute name, or list of names, whose values must be equal for matched edges. [limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stop after this many occurrences. If `None` (default), return all of them, which can be very many for large graphs and symmetric patterns. [symmetry]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return one mapping per occurrence up to the pattern's symmetries: mappings that differ only by an automorphism of the pattern (such as the 6 ways of matching a triangle's corners) are reported once. The search skips the symmetric copies rather than filtering them afterwards, so it is also faster. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[dict[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One dictionary per occurrence, mapping pattern node IDs to node IDs of this graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If one graph is directed and the other is not. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Uses the VF2++ style search of `is_isomorphic()`, enumerating every complete mapping. The number of occurrences, and therefore the running time, can grow exponentially with the pattern size. The mappings go from pattern to this graph, the reverse of NetworkX's `GraphMatcher(G, pattern).subgraph_isomorphisms_iter()`, which yields graph-to-pattern dictionaries; the occurrences themselves are the same. With `symmetry=True`, the symmetry breaking of ISMAGS (Houbraken et al., 2014) is used: the pattern's automorphism group is summarized by its cosets (see `automorphism_cosets()`), and each node must map to a smaller target node ID than the other nodes in its coset. Exactly one mapping per class of symmetric equivalents satisfies these constraints (Grochow and Kellis, 2007), so the count is the full count divided by the number of automorphisms of the pattern. With `induced=True` the occurrences are those of NetworkX's `ISMAGS(G, pattern).find_isomorphisms()`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~is_subgraph_isomorphic`) : Check whether the pattern occurs at all. [](`~automorphism_cosets`) : The symmetries that `symmetry=True` skips. [](`~largest_common_subgraph`) : The largest part of a pattern that does occur. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every feed-forward loop (`A` → `B` → `C` plus the shortcut `A` → `C`) in a small directed network, as mappings from the pattern's nodes: ::: {#b34dc4ba .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("x", "y"), ("y", "z"), ("x", "z"), ("z", "w"), ("y", "w")], directed=True ) loop = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("A", "C")], directed=True) [ {loop.get_label_from_id(p): graph.get_label_from_id(t) for p, t in m.items()} for m in graph.subgraph_isomorphisms(loop) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [{'A': 'x', 'B': 'y', 'C': 'z'}, {'A': 'y', 'B': 'z', 'C': 'w'}] ``` ::: ::: A square has 8 symmetries (4 rotations, each with or without a reflection): ::: {#7bc7a01a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} square = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(4) len(square.subgraph_isomorphisms(square)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 8 ``` ::: ::: A complete graph on four nodes holds 4 triangles, and each is found 6 times, once per way of matching its corners. With `symmetry=True`, each is found once: ::: {#4bdee6cc .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} k4 = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(4) triangle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(3) ( len(k4.subgraph_isomorphisms(triangle)), len(k4.subgraph_isomorphisms(triangle, symmetry=True)), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (24, 4) ``` ::: ::: ### Functional groups in caffeine A pattern can be a piece of a molecule. A carbonyl group is a carbon with a double bond to an oxygen. With `node_attr="element"` and `edge_attr="bond"`, the matches must agree on elements and bonds, and caffeine has two: ::: {#5e8a1231 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} caffeine = ec.molecules()["caffeine"] carbonyl = ec.Graph.from_edges([("C", "O")]) carbonyl.set_node_attrs("element", {"C": "C", "O": "O"}) carbonyl.set_edge_attrs("bond", {1: "double"}) matches = caffeine.subgraph_isomorphisms(carbonyl, node_attr="element", edge_attr="bond") [{carbonyl.get_label_from_id(p): caffeine.get_label_from_id(t) for p, t in m.items()} for m in matches] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [{'C': 'C5', 'O': 'O1'}, {'C': 'C6', 'O': 'O2'}] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#ece92179 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} caffeine.plot( color_by="element", highlight=[tuple(m.values()) for m in matches], label_by="label", edge_label_by="bond", seed=1, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Rings are cycles. With `symmetry=True`, a ring of five atoms and a ring of six are each found once. A ring of nine, around the outside of both, is found only with `induced=False`, since the bond C3–C4 that the two rings share cuts across it: ::: {#70169821 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} rings = { size: caffeine.subgraph_isomorphisms(ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(size), symmetry=True) for size in [5, 6, 9] } outer = caffeine.subgraph_isomorphisms( ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(9), induced=False, symmetry=True ) {size: len(found) for size, found in rings.items()}, len(outer) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` ({5: 1, 6: 1, 9: 0}, 1) ``` ::: ::: The five-atom ring is in full color, and the four atoms that only the six-atom ring adds are ringed: ::: {#56e4b04f .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} five = list(rings[5][0].values()) six = [node for node in rings[6][0].values() if node not in five] caffeine.plot( color_by="element", highlight={"accent": five, "soft": six}, label_by="label", seed=1 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
